edits.modify_from: For each rotating pair, estimate its shared center and follow both members' angular progression around that center across intermediate frames. Resolve the two identities jointly, continuing the observed rotation direction rather than independently choosing nearest endpoints. Returning to the same unordered pair of positions does not establish that identities returned: a half-turn exchanges them, and each successive observed exchange must be applied.
edits.modify_to: Seed target identities from the incoming positions at the start of the observed interval; for newly covered cubes, use the association with their descending covers. For each rotating pair, temporarily track both members, including any non-target partner. Estimate their shared center. At each successive observed frame, compare the two possible joint assignments of the pair's identities to its observed members, selecting the assignment consistent with the angular direction established by the preceding motion rather than independently minimizing endpoint distance. Carry the resulting identities into the next frame and through the final settling frames. Returning to the same unordered pair of positions must not reset identities: one observed half-turn exchanges them, and two observed half-turns restore them. Apply this procedure to each subsequent moving pair, carrying forward any target identity from earlier exchanges even when its partner changes. These temporary partner tracks do not add persistent memory fields. Perform this tracking even when the button count already determines the next command, and preserve the remaining targets' goal order when writing their updated positions.

revision.refused: No individual coordinate paths, color-specific cases, button-specific shuffle rules, or hard-coded endpoints are added. The shared frame-by-frame joint-assignment procedure covers these cases without assuming that every button press swaps a pair. No additional persistent field is needed. The annotator prompt, successful-lift removal rule, buttons_completed updates, and exclusive subgoal dispatch remain unchanged; the reported failures concern tracking identities, not those definitions or transitions.
